title: Why You Can't Remember Being A Baby
sources: Yale News, 20 Mar 2025: 'Why don't we remember being a baby? New study provides clues' (Yates et al., Science 387: hippocampal encoding of memories in human infants; infants about 1 year and older; retrieval may be the bottleneck) https://news.yale.edu/2025/03/20/why-dont-we-remember-being-baby-new-study-provides-clues
NPR, 20 Mar 2025: 'Why don't we remember being babies? Brain scans reveal new clues' https://www.npr.org/sections/shots-health-news/2025/03/20/nx-s1-5332387/baby-brain-scans-new-clues-infant-memories
Scientific American: 'We Make Memories as Babies, So Why Do We Forget Them?' https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/babies-do-make-memories-so-why-cant-we-remember-them-as-adults/

lines.text: Your baby brain was recording memories, and you can't find a single one.
lines.caps: YOUR BABY *BRAIN | WAS *RECORDING | YOU CAN'T FIND *ONE

lines.text: Most adults remember nothing from before about age three.
For decades, scientists thought baby brains simply couldn't store memories.
Then in 2025, Yale researchers scanned babies' brains while they looked at pictures.
When the memory center lit up brighter, the baby was more likely to recognize that picture later.
So the memories were being saved, in babies as young as one.
lines.caps: THE MEMORIES WERE *SAVED | IN BABIES AS YOUNG AS *ONE

lines.text: The real problem may be finding them again.
It's like a library where the books are on the shelves, but nobody can look them up.
lines.caps: A *LIBRARY | BOOKS ON THE *SHELVES | NO WAY TO *LOOK UP

lines.text: Scientists are still testing how long baby memories last.
So somewhere inside you, your first birthday may still be saved.
lines.caps: SOMEWHERE *INSIDE YOU | YOUR FIRST *BIRTHDAY | MAY BE *SAVED
